RenderObject.note: embedded per-car render object; [0]=back-ptr to veh base (live-verified slot16 gfx[0]==0x6352D8), [1]=scene root, [547]COCKPIT [548]SUSPENSION [549]HELMET [550]ARMS [551]BODY [552]WHEEL node ptrs (VehicleGraphicsSceneLoader_004dfce0)

FrontWingRecordPtr.note: Front-wing damage record, pointer. Armed by RepairServiceStateDispatcher_004ed250 case 4 (partIdx 4 = front wing) via ConditionalResourceRelease(this+818). Paired flag at 0xD14. Tested by StateTransition only, NOT by PitStopBlockingCondition_0042aee0 -- this is why a front-wing loss is REPAIRED at the box, not retired. Live 2026-07-24: slot 1 M.Schumacher, hook-proven partIdx 4, flag 1->0 on detach, 0->1 after the pit stop, car rejoined. Record stride is 0x44 (next record = rear wing at 0xD18). See investigations/part_detach_commentary/README.md.

FrontWingIntactFlag.note: Byte flag paired with 0xCD4 (delta 0x40). 1 = intact, 0 = armed/damaged (source tests it as !*(_BYTE*)). Live-observed 1->0 on front-wing detach and 0->1 after repair.

RearWingRecordPtr.note: Rear-wing damage record, pointer. Armed by RepairServiceStateDispatcher_004ed250 case 5 (partIdx 5 = rear wing) via ConditionalResourceRelease(this+835). Paired flag at 0xD58. THE RETIREMENT TRIGGER: PitStopBlockingCondition_0042aee0 returns true on `*(veh+0xD18) && !*(byte*)(veh+0xD58)`, which makes PitStopDecisionTireCompound_0042a3d0 write RetiredFlag(0x4410)=1 + ActiveFlag(0x45F4)=0 at the pit box. Live 2026-07-24: slot 7 Raikkonen, hook-proven partIdx 5, flag 1->0 on detach, callToBox 0->1 within 0.4s, retired at the box. Wheel loss does NOT arm this (cases 0-3 never touch this+835). Flag RESETS to 1 once the retirement completes -- only observable between detach and pit box.

RearWingIntactFlag.note: Width correction: the game tests and writes this as a byte. Zero plus CallToBox enters the game-owned garage/retirement path.

RenderMode.note: = RenderObject+0x964; render/detail mode 0..3 written by sub_4E0ED0; PitCrewStateMachine_004bbfc0 reads it to pass as a2

DriverModelVisible.note: = RenderObject+0x96D. byte 1=driver drawn, 0=hidden. Gates HELMET(549)/ARMS(550)/BODY(551) in sub_4E0ED0. POKE-PROVEN 2026-07-24 on slot16 M.SALO (0x636335 1->0): helmet+arms vanished on screen, car kept driving; poke persists (not rewritten per-frame). PitCrewStateMachine_004bbfc0 clears it on the pit/retire branch, sets 1 on exit. THIS is the driver-removal step of a real retirement. Poke-persistence re-verified 2026-07-24 side-by-side with 0x1065: 0x105D holds after a write, 0x1065 is overwritten every frame.

ParkingBrakeIndicator.note: = RenderObject+0x975. byte. OUTPUT, NOT AN INPUT — poke-DISPROVEN 2026-07-24: writing 1 on a healthy moving car (E.TesterA) succeeds but is reverted to 0 within 0.5 s. VehiclePhysicsTimeStep_004c73f0:165 recomputes it EVERY FRAME from packed word bit 0x4000000: v27=(netword+56 & 0x4000000)!=0; this[0x1065]=v27; if v27 then BrakeFactor(0x3584)=1.0f. So it MIRRORS the braking state, it does not cause it. Reads 1 on retired cars / 0 on running cars, so it is a reliable retirement INDICATOR. Writing it in a retire recipe is a no-op. Contrast DriverModelVisible(0x105D), decoded from bit 0x8000000 of the same word, which DOES latch when poked.

WearTickGate__was__slot_live_marker_.note: Controller/liveness role used by field construction: -1 inactive, 0 human, 1 AI, 2 remote. The multiplayer-AI prototype may temporarily park its own positively identified slots at -1 while stock network-slot cleanup runs, then restore 1 and rebuild the active pointer array on the same game-thread call. Never apply this to an unowned slot.

aiPitStrategyIndex.note: Pit-strategy index selecting the AIPit08/09/10 commentary: AIFormationLap switches case 1->eid 180 ('1 stop strategy'), 2->181 ('2 stop'), 3->182 ('3 stop'). Sole reader in the corpus is AIFormationLap; no writer found. Live mid-race it reads 3 on ALL 12 active slots including the player, which is the mechanism behind the known 'AIPit10 fires on 1-stoppers' bug.

tirePuncture_RR.note: Offset/field (tire wear-rate) is CONFIRMED, but the game itself does NOT simulate tire punctures natively. F1CUI fakes a puncture by driving this wear-rate field to minimum externally; the 'puncture' semantic is an F1CUI-side interpretation, not a native in-game mechanic. User-reported correction, 2026-07-24. Live poke this session (severe collision, no F1CUI running) moved this field by only ~0.0001 (1.0->0.9999), consistent with normal physics jitter, not a real puncture-scale event. LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-25 (Frida read of both int and float interpretations, in-race, mods/f1cui_web_remote debugging session): Confirmed to behave as TIRE WEAR (remaining tread, 1.0 = fresh): lap 1 readings RR were 1.0 on a stationary car and 0.99998 (front) / 0.99999 (rear) on a running car, fronts wearing faster. Moves ~2e-4 per lap, so any display with fewer than 4 decimals looks frozen.

FuelLevel.note: Located 2026-07-25 by time-series drift analysis over ~28s of green-flag running, 21 cars (tools/engine_temp_poll.js). DISCRIMINATOR: cars with a dead engine (Schumacher, Hakkinen -- rpm 0 and EngineAngVel 0) held these values EXACTLY frozen (delta 0.000) while every running car drifted. DECREASES steadily while running (-0.56..-0.96 per 28s) and is frozen when stopped -- litres of fuel remaining. Observed 124-149 at a race start, consistent with a 2001 refuelling-era load. Distinct from fuelConsumption (+0x3990), which is a per-lap RATE; this is the remaining quantity, which the corpus did not previously expose. Not poke-proven.

OilTemp.note: Located 2026-07-25 by time-series drift analysis over ~28s of green-flag running, 21 cars (tools/engine_temp_poll.js). DISCRIMINATOR: cars with a dead engine (Schumacher, Hakkinen -- rpm 0 and EngineAngVel 0) held these values EXACTLY frozen (delta 0.000) while every running car drifted. Rises steadily while the engine runs (+0.03..+0.08 per 28s). Two clusters (~84 and ~100) are NOT health -- they are different engine manufacturers, since each team has its own SeasonData/Vehicles/<team>/engine.ini with a different OptimumOilTemp (Arrows 2001 = 105.6). Montoya/Raikkonen/TesterA sit at ~84 while running perfectly. RELIABILITY RELEVANCE: engine.ini LifetimeOilTemp=(123.43,2.90) halves remaining engine life for every 2.90C above 123.43, so this is a real wear lever, not cosmetic. Not poke-proven.

WaterTemp.note: Located 2026-07-25 by time-series drift analysis over ~28s of green-flag running, 21 cars (tools/engine_temp_poll.js). DISCRIMINATOR: cars with a dead engine (Schumacher, Hakkinen -- rpm 0 and EngineAngVel 0) held these values EXACTLY frozen (delta 0.000) while every running car drifted. Same drift signature as OilTemp (0x3D10) at lower magnitude (~52-58 vs ~84-101), consistent with engine.ini OilWaterHeatTransfer/WaterMinimumCooling modelling water as a separate cooler circuit. Not poke-proven.

carConditions.note: Live-poked on player slot, 2026-07-24: value is a damage-severity level, not a boolean. Wings-only crash (FW+RW off, wheel intact) -> 0->1. Wheel-loss crash (FW+RW+RF wheel off) -> 0->2. Two independent trials. See mods/ai_wing_retire/README.md session update. PROMOTED CONFIRMED->FACT 2026-07-24: Frida hook on RepairServiceStateDispatcher_004ed250 + sub_41AFD0_0041afd0 (tools/part_detach_watch.js) logged the raw partIdx argument on an AI car (slot 20 Webber). partIdx 5 (rear wing) + 6/9/10 (bodywork) -> carConditions 0->1 with ReasonCode untouched at 0; wheel cases (partIdx 0-3) are the only path that writes ReasonCode=6 and are the only path observed to give carConditions=2. Severity semantics: 1 = wing/bodywork, 2 = wheel loss. NOTE: value is NOT exclusively wheel-derived at 2 -- slot 8 Trulli observed at carConditions=2 with ReasonCode=8 (electronics), so 2 is reachable by non-detach paths too.

sources: live:investigations/engine_lifetime 2026-07-25 (armed on an AI, in-game confirmed)
EngineLifeRemaining.note: COMPONENT LIFE COUNTDOWN, seconds remaining. FuelConsumptionAndWear_004ed960 decrements four of these by delta-time each tick (`this[i+3929] -= a2` for i=0..3, gated on sub_4D21D0) and when one goes negative writes the matching ReasonCode into veh+0x4068 and fails that component. NOTE the decompiled `this` is veh+0xC, NOT the vehicle base, so index 3929 resolves to veh+0x3D70. Live: healthy cars read 20000-41000 s; a car whose engine had just blown read -1.0 in the engine slot. POKE-PROVEN 2026-07-25: writing 0.5 to the engine slot on a healthy running AI (Sarrazin) fired ReasonCode=1 within 0.2 s, the engine wound down 1577->0 rpm, and 5 s later the GAME ITSELF set FinishState=2 + RetiredFlag=1. Arming this trigger produces a genuine failure; no state is forged. Distinct from OilTemp (0x3D10), which is only a readout -- pinning it at 200 C for 24 s did nothing. This slot fires ReasonCode 1 Engine. AI-ONLY: the decrement is gated on veh+0x32C8==1, which is 0 for the human driver (see 0x32C8). FULL-RACE MEASUREMENT 2026-07-25: drains at exactly 1.000/s for all 21 simulated cars over 65 minutes, unaffected by oil temp (101->113 C) or revs, and keeps draining on a car that has already retired. It is a plain wall clock. Lowest value reached in a 53-lap race was 10400 s, so AI components can never fail from this counter within a race distance -- scripted failures via the veh+0x4144 table are the only path.

plannedPositionAtStart.note: Starting-grid slot consumed by the placement path (sub_4D10E0 -> sub_403CD0(gridTable, plannedPositionAtStart-1)). Prior art: moving a car on the grid requires writing this field AND vehicle+0x4060 together; writing only 0x4058 leaves the car on pole. Reviewed as a latched control input for the multiplayer qualifying-grid fix; writes must keep positions a contiguous 1..n permutation.

position.note: Race position ordered by standings and the visible grid; the second field required to move a car on the starting grid (see 0x4058). Reviewed as a latched control input for the multiplayer qualifying-grid fix; writes must keep positions a contiguous 1..n permutation.

ReasonCode.note: AI-CLASSIFICATION LABEL ONLY, not a live damage signal. Per the game owner (2026-07-25) these codes exist solely to fill in AI mechanical-failure reasons on the final classification screen; the player's own failure modes (brake failure, engine failure from mechanical or impact damage, bodywork loss) are not represented here. Consistent with: NOT written by the pit-retirement path — stayed 0 across a genuine AI retirement (live-observed AI rear-wing pit retirement, M.SALO slot16, 2026-07-24) and across all three rear-wing retirements in mods/investigations/part_detach_commentary. Only partIdx 0-3 (wheel) writes it, as =6. Earlier 'set ReasonCode=6' guidance came from an ACCIDENT capture and does not generalize. Read it only for cars already classified out; it is meaningless mid-race.

PitDecisionTimer.note: Set to zero after scheduling a stop to make the AI evaluate the request.

SteeringLaneMode0.note: Lane/conflict mode slot 0 in the five-entry 28-byte AISteering state array. Modes 1/2/7/8 reach Overtaking; mode 16 is the follow/fallback state. Read-only in the pass-commitment prototype.

SteeringLanePressure0.note: AISteering pass-pressure/history slot 0. Accumulates closing traffic weighted by TrackAggressionEffective, clamps to 0..450, and retains 85 percent on transition to mode 16. Live trace reproduced 450 to 382.5.

CurrentWaypointPtr.note: Pointer to the AI's current waypoint struct. Static: sub_426430 line 76 does a fresh SpatialNearestNeighborQueryWithPlaneTest when this is NULL, and line 87 only re-queries a non-NULL one if the car is >3200 (squared, ~57 m) from it; the struct is deref'd at +0x94/+0x9C (world X/Y), +0x110 normal successor, +0x114 alternate successor, +0x12C pit-entry flag. POKE-PROVEN 2026-07-25: a garaged car holding a STALE pointer (M.Schumacher) drove 16 m into the garage wall at a pre-retirement racing-line node; writing 0 here on a car with the identical failing signature (Frentzen, wp=0x367895d8, lane=0) made it re-query and drive the pit lane out, 905 m, gear 5. Repopulates within 1.5 s after being nulled. See investigations/garage_exit_ignition/README.md.

QualifyingAbilityNorm.note: LIVE VALUE-MATCHED 2026-07-27, 21/21 cars: = (22 - rcd QualifyingAbility)/22 (fit slope -0.045455 = -1/22, intercept 1.0). The qualifying twin of RaceAbilityNorm (0x44C4) but WITHOUT the quadratic AI-difficulty-slider damping: 0x44C4 carries a x(slider/100)^2 factor (0.8464 at slider 92) and this one does not. Lower raw ability = higher norm = faster.

RaceAbilityNorm.note: LIVE-CONFIRMED 2026-07-26: (22 - RaceAbility)/22 x (AIDifficultySlider/100)^2, verified on 8 drivers (RA 1.8..10.6) at slider 92 with residual < 0.001 -- quadratic slider damping exact at 0.8464. CLAMPS AT 1.0: Alonso (effective RA ~ -82 in memory) reads exactly 1.0 while his unclamped 0x44F4 runs to 1.7504. Lower raw RA = higher norm = faster. Baked once at session init; feed for the per-frame pace walk at 0x453C. NOTE: effective RA can differ from the loose SeasonData rcd when a randomizer/save pipeline is active (Webber ~7.30 vs file 11.3) -- both formulas still hold with the effective value.  CORROBORATED 2026-07-27 by an independent method (live affine value-match vs the shipped .rcd files, tools/match_values.py): 21/21 cars fit 0.8464 - 0.038473 x RaceAbility, which is algebraically identical to 0.8464 x (22 - RaceAbility)/22 and recovers the (92/100)^2 = 0.8464 slider term without being told it. No clamping and no randomizer divergence in this session.

RainAbilityScaled.note: LIVE VALUE-MATCHED 2026-07-27, 21/21 cars: = rcd RainAbility /100 x GlobalDifficultyScalar(0x5EA3D8) (fit slope 0.0096 = 0.01 x 0.96 at slider 92, intercept ~0). Same /100 x scalar shape as AbilityBaselineScalar (0x44F4) but NOT inverted - 0x44F4 uses (1 - RA/100), this uses RainAbility/100 directly, so here a HIGHER raw value gives a higher field.

PassingNorm.note: Baked AI Passing tuning input: .rcd Passing maps to 0.9 + Passing*0.001, capped at 1.0. AIRacingLine consumes it in the gap/line calculation; initialization may replace it. Game-thread temporary overrides must capture/restore by vehicle identity and session, use finite 0.9..1.0 values, and yield at session teardown. This is a latched tuning input, not computed scoring output.

CrashPct.note: LIVE VALUE-MATCHED 2026-07-27, 21/21 cars: stored as the raw rcd Crash percentage, identity transform (slope 1.0, intercept ~0). Observed range 2.4..31.2 on the 2001 grid.

RaceAbilityNormPush.note: RELATION IS CONFIRMED, THE NAME IS NOT. Live value-matched 2026-07-27, 21/21 cars: = 1 - 0.030455 x rcd RaceAbility, and 0.030455 = 0.67/22 exactly, so the field is 1 - 0.67 x (RaceAbility/22). Written by sub_424080, read by AIAbility_00429470 (both via ask.py). Previously unnamed and absent from the .rcd files as a token, so it is COMPUTED at parse time, not parsed. The 'push' reading is inference from the 0.67 constant, which is the same push/attack coefficient documented on 0x44F4 (push target = base + (1-base) x 0.67) - treat the semantic label as unproven.

RaceAbilityPushScalar.note: RELATION IS CONFIRMED, THE NAME IS NOT. Live value-matched 2026-07-27, 21/21 cars: = 0.0268 + 0.006432 x rcd RaceAbility, which factors exactly as 0.67 x (0.04 + 0.0096 x RaceAbility) - the same 0.67 push coefficient and the same 0.0096 = 0.01 x GlobalDifficultyScalar seen on 0x44C8/0x44F4. Written by sub_424080; read by AIAbility_00429470 AND AIPushLap_0042a180 (via ask.py). The AIPushLap reader makes this a candidate AI push/qualifying-run knob - UNEXPLORED, no poke test yet. Computed at parse time, not an .rcd token.

CompletedLapsPct.note: LIVE VALUE-MATCHED 2026-07-27, 21/21 cars: stored as the raw rcd 'CompletedLaps%' percentage, identity transform. Only 4 distinct values on the 2001 grid (60..90), so the live match is weaker evidence here than for the others - it rests mainly on the static token->offset pair from sub_424080.

AbilityBaselineScalar.note: LIVE-CONFIRMED 2026-07-26: (1 - RaceAbility/100) x GlobalDifficultyScalar(0x5EA3D8, 0.96 at slider 92), exact to float precision on all sampled drivers (Schumacher 0.94272, De La Rosa 0.85824). Steady-state target of the live pace factor 0x453C: Schumacher's 0x453C settled exactly on 0.94272 during green running. Push/attack target = this + (1 - this) x 0.67 (De La Rosa observed parked exactly on 0.953219 = 0.85824 + 0.14176 x 0.67). NOT clamped (Alonso 1.7504 in one corrupted session bake; next session he baked normally at 0.84288 = file RA 12.2 -- the anomaly is SESSION-SCOPED, not persistent). MID-SESSION INTERVENTION POINT, POKE-PROVEN 2026-07-26: this field is READ every frame by AIAbility but never rewritten during a session -- writing it mid-race sticks, and 0x453C walks to the new value at the game's own +-0.01/frame (Salo in-race: baseline 0.88128 -> 0.85128, pace factor followed over ~8 s, on-screen natural). Tool: tools/ai_live_form.py (docs/43 sec3.8).  CORROBORATED 2026-07-27 by an independent method (live affine value-match vs the shipped .rcd files, tools/match_values.py): 21/21 cars fit 0.96 - 0.0096 x RaceAbility, algebraically identical to (1 - RaceAbility/100) x 0.96, independently pinning GlobalDifficultyScalar(0x5EA3D8) = 0.96 at slider 92.

TrackAggressionEffective.note: Baked AI follow-gap/pressure tuning input: AI Realism times TrackAggression, floored at 0.01 during initialization; AISteering consumes it without recomputing the input. Game-thread finite temporary controls require identity/session ownership and exact restoration. Classification does not authorize arbitrary ranges or make this a no-passing switch.

MaxSpeed.note: Not a raw poke: the field recalculates every frame, so the write is always the game's own ParameterValueSetter thiscall (a2 cast straight to float, 18 = pit-limit sentinel, 99999 = uncapped), re-armed every tick by the caller, gated on race_phase==5 the same as CallToBox. Never govern a car whose PitStatus (0x3450) != 0 -- that overwrites the game's own pit limiter.

LivePaceFactor.note: LIVE-CONFIRMED 2026-07-26: per-frame pace factor, walked +/-0.01/frame toward a baked target. Observed: Schumacher settled at his 0x44F4 baseline (0.94272, one -0.01 step from 0.95272 seen at 4 Hz); De La Rosa parked exactly at his attack target baseline+boost (0.953219). RECOMPUTED EVERY FRAME -- external pokes do NOT persist; intervene via 0x44C4/0x44F4 right after session init or via the rcd. Alonso (effective RA ~ -82) reads 2.1, above any documented target -- pathological effective-RA case.

WaypointSetSelector.note: 3rd arg passed to SpatialNearestNeighborQueryWithPlaneTest (sub_426430 lines 78/89) selecting which waypoint node set the nearest-neighbour query searches; line 138 REWRITES it every frame from the acquired waypoint's +0x12C, so it is an output as much as an input. Also gates the pit-speed target (line 145: value 1 forces flt_8ACFB4). NOT a lap counter -- the 'PitLapCounter' name in AIMainUpdate_00424e70.md prose is wrong. DO NOT read it as 'car is in the pit lane': live 2026-07-25, Frentzen drove the entire pit-lane corridor reading 0 while Raikkonen drove the same corridor reading 1. REFUTED as a de-retirement input -- seeding 1 is a no-op because a garaged car often already reads 1. Exact semantics of the set index unresolved.

elapsedTime.note: SUSPECT: reads 0.0 for every car, every session checked (verified live 2026-07-25 across 22 cars mid-race). Do NOT use for gaps or race time -- use totalTimeOnFinishLine (+0x4098), which IS per-car cumulative. Trust tag left at CONFIRMED because the disagreement is with observed behaviour rather than a second naming source, but treat this offset and its neighbourhood as unreliable; 0x4574 next door is a damage flag, not time data.

Unknown_4574.note: DISPROVEN as an engine-seize / heavy-impact flag. LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-25 (Frida read of both int and float interpretations, in-race, mods/f1cui_web_remote debugging session): At the START of a race with every car pristine and damage.ini wings disabled, slots 3 (Coulthard) and 5 (TesterA) already read 1 while slots 0/1/2/4 read 0. A seize flag cannot be set on an undamaged stationary car. Static per-car property of unknown meaning. Previously fed into a 'DOOMED / ENGINE STOPPED' prognosis, which is why healthy cars were reported as doomed. Supersedes investigations/engine_seize/ provisional claim.

AIControlFlag.note: Previously named activeFlag/'on track'.  LIVE-DISPROVEN 2026-07-25 (mods/f1cui_web_remote): Reads 0 for the HUMAN driver while racing (slot 0, P1, 79 km/h, finishState 0, retired 0) and 1 for every AI car; a retired AI drops to 0. It is an AI-control bit, not presence. Consequences seen: a map filtered on it never drew the player's car, and a pit heuristic of `!flag && !retired && fs==0` matched ONLY the human, flagging them as pitting for a whole race. For presence use `finishState==0 && !RetiredFlag`. Note the retirement writer PitStopDecisionTireCompound_0042a3d0 writes 0 here alongside RetiredFlag=1, which is consistent: the AI stops driving it.

DynMan_Init.abi_evidence: Raw function has no receiver or arguments; all call sites use a plain call. Canonical bytes begin with one complete six-byte stack-allocation instruction (81 EC 0C 02 00 00).

DynMan_Restart.abi_evidence: Exact canonical SHA256 executable disassembled over 0x42C3B0..0x42C439 and caller Game_Restart. No incoming ECX/EDX or stack arguments are read; ECX is overwritten before use; return is EAX and plain C3 ret. Caller supplies no stack arguments (its ECX assignment is unused by this callee). First instruction is the complete five-byte push 0x26f (68 6F 02 00 00). Reviewed as no-argument cdecl; not authorized as a standalone arbitrary restart command. See tools/sdk/SAFETY_CAR_INTERFACE_REVIEW_2026-09-07.md.

ProcessDriverEntries.abi_evidence: The two recovered callers pass the driver-entry manager in ecx with no stack arguments. The callee returns its final vehicle-bound pointer in eax. Canonical entry begins with one complete six-byte stack-allocation instruction.

TeamIDSetter.abi_evidence: Raw twelve-line callee directly writes the one stack argument into five fields on the ecx vehicle. Two static callers and native safety-car live construction agree.

SceneRenderUpdate.abi_evidence: Seven recovered callers pass a vehicle in ecx and one 32-bit stack value consumed as a byte. The callee initializes physics, render, AI driver and collision state for that vehicle.

SessionStateTransition.abi_evidence: The explicit callers in NetCommPlayerSlotSync, RestartGate, and sub_4DA840 pass F1CVehicle+0x0C in ecx; ProcessDriverEntries constructs the same interior owner as v24+3 dwords. The callee reads its controller role at owner+0x32BC, which resolves to the canonical vehicle role at +0x32C8. Two 32-bit stack arguments are passed and the second is consumed as a byte. Passing the vehicle base corrupts the preceding controller field and is forbidden.

AIDriverCountSetup.abi_evidence: The sole caller DynMan_Init pushes one path pointer and the callee returns with ret 4. The raw callee is stdcall, returns zero in eax, and is the last identity/count stage before DynMan_Init rebuilds the active array and runs its counted VehgenScnFileLoader loop. Canonical entry starts with the complete five-byte mov eax,[VehicleCount] instruction.

SuspensionForceComputationWithPerCornerV.abi_evidence: The sole caller RenderTickUpdate passes active_vehicle+20 in ecx with no stack arguments and consumes the byte result in al. The callee uses ecx as its dynamics owner, has no stack parameters, and returns a byte. Canonical entry begins with complete instructions 83 EC 24 56 8B F1.

MultiplayerQualificationGridAssignment.abi_evidence: The sole caller MultiplayerVehiclePlacement passes the session manager in ecx with no stack arguments and consumes the byte result in al. The callee uses the receiver throughout and returns the local-player-found byte. Canonical and reviewed DE151845 variant entries both begin with complete instructions 83 EC 10 55 56.

ConditionalFieldSetter.abi_evidence: Seven recovered callers pass the per-vehicle grid-state owner in ecx and one 32-bit position on the stack. The callee compares and writes that value and has no return value.

FieldCopy.abi_evidence: Three recovered callers pass the per-vehicle grid-state owner in ecx with no stack arguments. The callee copies the current position into plannedPositionAtStart and returns that 32-bit position in eax.

VehgenScnFileLoader.abi_evidence: Three callers pass a vehicle in ecx and one 32-bit stack argument; raw callee uses this and a byte value and returns a char pointer. Native safety-car load trials exercised this ABI on the game thread.

NetCommPlayerSlotSync.abi_evidence: Sole caller passes the network manager in ecx; callee has no stack arguments and returns its result in al. Canonical prologue preserves a thiscall frame.

VehicleLookupByName.abi_evidence: Raw callee and seven callers agree on stdcall with one path pointer; result is written to the canonical roster-index global.

NationalityDriverInfoLoader.abi_evidence: Confirmed F1CVehicle owner; raw callee and four callers agree on thiscall plus one roster-index argument. The same ABI was exercised by the native safety-car load-time prototype.

MultiplayerVehiclePlacement.abi_evidence: Canonical disassembly at 0x42CF10 begins push ebx; push ebp; push esi; mov ebp,ecx; push edi - thiscall receiver plus one stack argument. Raw Hex-Rays is int __thiscall sub_42CF10(_DWORD *this, int a2); a2==5 runs the per-vehicle FieldCopy pass, a2==7 runs the grid reorder (ChampionshipStandingsReOrdering or sub_462E20) then FieldCopy_c330 per vehicle. CommentaryEventQueue.abi_evidence: Canonical disassembly at 0x4144F0 begins mov eax,[esp+8]; mov edx,[esp+0xc]; push esi; mov esi,ecx - thiscall receiver plus six integer/float stack arguments, return ignored (void). Raw Hex-Rays is void __thiscall sub_4144F0(float *this, int a2, int a3, int a4, int a5, int a6, float a7, float a8). Every commentary emitter calls it to queue an event id plus optional driver ids. Diagnostic logging only.

CommentaryDriverEntryInit.abi_evidence: Canonical executable disassembly at 0x414600 begins with the complete six-byte sub esp,0x100 and mov esi,ecx thiscall receiver; raw Hex-Rays is int __thiscall sub_414600(const char **this, char a2). It builds the pws/tv audio keys per catalog record and calls DriverNameIDLookup per slot. Called only from NamedEntryLookupInFormatList and VehicleListBuilderFromGlobalArray. Used by the callout fix to fill unresolved driver slots after the stock pass.

CommentaryNameListRebuild.abi_evidence: Raw Hex-Rays is int __thiscall sub_415090(void *this); the sole caller LazyRendererAudioInitCheck passes &dword_5EA5E8 in ECX and ignores only the status return. It rebuilds the commentary name/audio lists by calling VehicleListBuilderFromGlobalArray, NameListBuilderFromVehicleArray and SceneListBuilderFromGlobalArray, which run DriverNameIDLookup per catalog record. DriverNameIDLookup.abi_evidence: Canonical executable disassembly at 0x415D90 begins with the complete five-byte push ebx; mov ebx,[esp+0x10] sequence and the raw Hex-Rays is declared int __stdcall sub_415D90(int a1, int a2, unsigned int a3, char a4, char a5) - five stack arguments, stdcall. It writes resolved ids to entry_field+8, +12 and +16 and compares the driver-name string at catalog record +188 against short names. Sole caller is the registration builder sub_414600. Read-only name resolution; used by the callout fix hook.
